To push code to a GitHub repository, you need to have Git installed on your machine and a GitHub account. Here are the steps:

1. Install Git: Download Git from the official website and follow the installation instructions for your operating system (Windows, macOS, or Linux).
2. Create a GitHub Account: Sign up for a free account at github.com.
3. Configure Git: Open your command line interface (CLI) or terminal and set your username and email using the following commands:
```
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "your_email@example.com"
```
4. Add your local repository to GitHub using Git: You can add your local repository to GitHub using Git by running the following command:
```
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit"
git push origin master
```
Replace "master" with the name of the branch you want to push.

Alternatively, you can use the GitHub CLI to push your commits. Pass the `--push` flag to the `git push` command to push your commits.

For more information about possible arguments, see the GitHub CLI manual.

You can also use Visual Studio Code or Visual Studio to push your code to GitHub. The steps are similar to the ones above, but you will need to use the VS Code or VS interface to authenticate and push your code.
